sentences.en: Programming Throwdown, episode 61, Clojure, with special guest Eric Norman.
sentences.zh: Programming Throwdown 播客第 61 期，今天的主角是 Clojure，特邀嘉宾是 Eric Normand。

sentences.en: Take it away, Jason.
sentences.zh: 请开始吧，Jason。

sentences.en: Hey, everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: If you're a longtime listener, you may remember we did an episode on Lisp almost three years ago.
sentences.zh: 如果你是我们的老听众，可能还记得差不多三年前我们做过一期关于 Lisp 的节目。

sentences.en: And we're coming back, and we're covering it in a lot of detail.
sentences.zh: 现在我们又回来了，这次我们要详细深入地探讨它。

sentences.en: One of the things, one of the comments that we got when we did the Lisp episode from a lot of people was, you know, hey, we want to learn more about Lisp.
sentences.zh: 当时我们在做完 Lisp 那期节目后，收到很多听众的反馈，大家都在说，嘿，我们想了解更多关于 Lisp 的知识。

sentences.en: And here's some more details about Lisp and things like that.
sentences.zh: 以及诸如此类关于 Lisp 的更多细节。

sentences.en: This is before we really had a strong social network presence, where the only way you could really communicate was by emailing us.
sentences.zh: 那是我们还没什么社交网络影响力的时期，当时唯一真正的交流方式就是给我们发邮件。

sentences.en: And so we got a lot of email about Lisp.
sentences.zh: 所以我们收到了大量关于 Lisp 的邮件。

sentences.en: And so we're really happy.
sentences.zh: 因此我们真的非常高兴。

sentences.en: Oh, go ahead, Patrick.
sentences.zh: 哦，请说，Patrick。

sentences.en: Yeah, we also briefly did mention Clojure.
sentences.zh: 对，我们当时也简短地提到过 Clojure。

sentences.en: We did like a collective episode of a bunch of JVM languages.
sentences.zh: 我们做过一期包含一堆 JVM 语言的综合节目。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so we mentioned Clojure by name there.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里直接提到了 Clojure。

sentences.en: And so we have Eric Normand to talk in much more detail about Clojure and kind of really teach all of us a lot of really cool things about Clojure.
sentences.zh: 所以我们这次请来了 Eric Normand，来跟我们更详细地聊聊 Clojure，并向我们所有人传授许多关于 Clojure 的超酷知识。

sentences.en: So, Eric, kind of tell us about yourself and what do you do?
sentences.zh: 那么，Eric，跟我们简单介绍一下你自己以及你的工作吧？

sentences.en: Hi, my name is Eric Normand.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我叫 Eric Normand。

sentences.en: My current tagline is I help people thrive with functional programming.
sentences.zh: 我目前的标语是：我帮助人们在函数式编程中取得成功。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: I run a site called purelyfunctional.tv where I teach people Clojure.
sentences.zh: 我运营着一个叫 purelyfunctional.tv 的网站，我在上面教人们 Clojure。

sentences.en: I want to expand it to other functional programming languages.
sentences.zh: 我想把它扩展到其他函数式编程语言。

sentences.en: And I basically teach with video and exercises and other online things.
sentences.zh: 我主要通过视频、练习和其他在线内容来进行教学。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: What sort of inspired you to build that site and to teach people Clojure and other functional languages?
sentences.zh: 是什么启发你去建立那个网站并教人们 Clojure 以及其他函数式语言的呢？

sentences.en: Well, it's evolved over time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个是随着时间慢慢演变而来的。

sentences.en: I have always liked teaching.
sentences.zh: 我一直都很喜欢教学。

sentences.en: Well, always.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一直都是。

sentences.en: I was a teacher in the Peace Corps.
sentences.zh: 我曾在和平队当过老师。

sentences.en: And I was teaching math.
sentences.zh: 我教的是数学。

sentences.en: And when I got back, I kind of started missing it.
sentences.zh: 等我回来后，我发现自己有点想念教学。

sentences.en: I started programming again.
sentences.zh: 我重新开始编程。

sentences.en: And I started making videos off and on.
sentences.zh: 然后我断断续续地开始制作视频。

sentences.en: And then at some point, I did a Kickstarter to get some Clojure videos made.
sentences.zh: 再后来，有段时间我在 Kickstarter 上发起了一次众筹，想要制作一些 Clojure 视频。

sentences.en: And that was a success.
sentences.zh: 结果很成功。

sentences.en: And just ever since then, I've been adding more and more videos.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我就一直在不断添加越来越多的视频。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: Very cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: What is it like running a Kickstarter?
sentences.zh: 运营一个 Kickstarter 项目是怎样的体验？

sentences.en: I've never actually funded several Kickstarters.
sentences.zh: 我其实从来没有，我资助过好几个 Kickstarter 项目。

sentences.en: I've never Kickstarted anything.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有在 Kickstarter 上发起过项目。

sentences.en: I mean, how do you, what was that process like?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你是怎么做到的，那个过程是怎样的？

sentences.en: So, it was not, I mean, it wasn't that big of a deal.
sentences.zh: 所以，其实也还好，我是说，没那么大不了。

sentences.en: I think the biggest thing was beforehand, I talked to my friend who has funded a lot and like kind of saw what worked and what didn't.
sentences.zh: 我想最重要的一点是，在开始之前，我跟一个资助过很多项目的朋友聊过，了解了什么行得通、什么行不通。

sentences.en: I hadn't been active on Kickstarter at all.
sentences.zh: 我之前完全没怎么用过 Kickstarter。

sentences.en: And so, it was like just a lot of discussions with him about like how, what should I set my goal at, what should my rewards be, you know, that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，我跟他讨论了很多，比如我的目标该设多少、回报应该是什么样的，你知道的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And he helped me come up with the structure there.
sentences.zh: 然后他帮我理清了那里的整体结构。

sentences.en: Cool.
sentences.zh: 酷。

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对。

sentences.en: I would say that my biggest advice for someone who's going to do a Kickstarter is take into account the marketing that you're going to do during the campaign.
sentences.zh: 我想说，对于准备在 Kickstarter 上发起项目的人，我最大的建议是：要把你在众筹期间要做的营销考虑进去。

sentences.en: So, I did mine for 30 days, which at that time was the default.
sentences.zh: 所以我的项目持续了 30 天，当时这是默认时长。

sentences.en: I don't know what the default is now.
sentences.zh: 我不知道现在默认是几天。

sentences.en: But at that time, it was default to 30 days.
sentences.zh: 但当时默认就是 30 天。

sentences.en: And so, that's 30 days of you like tweeting and promoting and like just being generally like on edge about whether you're going to make it and stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以，这意味着你要花 30 天发推特、进行宣传，并且整天处于焦虑之中，担心自己能不能成功筹到钱之类的。

sentences.en: And if I were to do it again, I would probably cut it down to like 10 days or 15 days.
sentences.zh: 如果让我再来一次，我可能会把它缩短到 10 天或 15 天左右。

sentences.en: Um, because most of the, the backers came in at either the beginning or the end.
sentences.zh: 因为绝大多数支持者要么在刚开始时出现，要么在快结束时出现。

sentences.en: And so, if you just cut out the middle, then I would have had about the same amount.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你把中间的时间切掉，我其实也能拿到差不多的金额。

sentences.en: So, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 原来如此，这倒说得通。

sentences.en: And one thing that I noticed is it's really, you know, you have to, the audience wants to have faith in, in you, like in you delivering on the Kickstarter.
sentences.zh: 我注意到的一点是，真的，你知道，你必须让受众对你产生信任，相信你能把 Kickstarter 项目做成并交付。

sentences.en: And so, if you're, if you're messaging every single day, like, you know, here's what I ate for breakfast today.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你每天都在发消息，比如，你知道，今天我早餐吃了什么。

sentences.en: I ate closure flavored Cheerios.
sentences.zh: 我吃了 Clojure 口味的雀巢奇瑞欧圈麦片。

sentences.en: Then, then like people know, okay, this person needs business.
sentences.zh: 那么，大家就会明白，好吧，这个人是认真的。

sentences.en: And, and if I, if I donate that it's one, it's going to work out.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果我进行捐赠，第一，这肯定能成。

sentences.en: And two, like I'm donating to more than just a set of videos.
sentences.zh: 第二，我捐赠的不只是几段视频。

sentences.en: It's like a cause.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一项事业。

sentences.en: Yeah, for sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: It really helps to have an audience before you start.
sentences.zh: 在开始之前就拥有受众真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: Um, I think that's the number one failure reason is, is people don't have anybody that, you know, who can listen, who knows, you know, they're shouting into the void.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为失败的首要原因就是，人们身边没有任何会听、会关注他们的人，他们就像是在对空呐喊。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实在理。

sentences.en: Um, so, so, you know, kind of explain, you know, if you had to sort of explain functional programming to someone who's never heard it before, how do you, you know, how do you
sentences.zh: 那么，能不能解释一下，如果你必须向一个从未听说过函数式编程的人解释它，你会怎么做？

sentences.en: sort of describe that?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么去描述它呢？

sentences.en: Let's say there's someone who, you know, has taken some courses, they get C, um, you know, and C++ really well.
sentences.zh: 假设对方上过一些课程，对 C 语言、嗯，还有 C++ 掌握得很好。

sentences.en: Um, and, but they've never seen Lisp or, or, or Haskell or, or Clojure or any of these.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是他们从来没见过 Lisp、Haskell、Clojure 或任何这些语言。

sentences.en: How would you sort of explain that to them?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么向他们解释呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So that's a really, uh, hard and complicated question because I don't think there is a very agreed upon definition of functional programming.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常难且复杂的问题，因为我觉得大家对函数式编程并没有一个公认的定义。

sentences.en: Um, but functional programming for sure comes from Lambda Calculus.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但函数式编程绝对源于拉姆达演算（Lambda Calculus）。

sentences.en: And Lambda Calculus is a mathematics that uses nothing but functions.
sentences.zh: 而拉姆达演算是一种只使用函数的数学体系。

sentences.en: And so there's definitely the notion of using functions as your main form of abstraction.
sentences.zh: 所以这里绝对有一个概念，就是把函数作为抽象的主要形式。

sentences.en: And functions are higher order.
sentences.zh: 而且函数是一等公民（高阶的）。

sentences.en: That means that they can be, uh, passed to other functions as arguments and you can return functions from arguments.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它们可以作为参数传递给其他函数，你也可以从函数中返回函数。

sentences.en: So functions are values that you can pass around and languages like C, C++, you can kind of, like, let's take C cause I know that a bit better.
sentences.zh: 因此函数是可以四处传递的值，而在像 C、C++ 这样的语言中，你有点——比如说 C 语言，因为我相对更熟悉一点。

sentences.en: You know, you can pass function pointers around and stuff and people do interesting stuff with that, but they don't have what's called lexical closures.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你可以传函数指针之类的东西，人们也用它做出了一些有趣的事情，但它们没有所谓的词法闭包（lexical closures）。

sentences.en: Uh, it's a technical term.
sentences.zh: 这是一个专业术语。

sentences.en: Uh, it just means a function that can refer to variables that are defined where the function is defined.
sentences.zh: 它只是指一个函数，能够引用在定义该函数时所处作用域中定义的变量。

sentences.en: So like in JavaScript, if I have a, um, a variable defined, let's say variable a equals one, and
sentences.zh: 所以就像在 JavaScript 中，如果我定义了一个，嗯，定义了一个变量，比方说变量 a 等于 1，然后

sentences.en: then I have a function defined right after that, then I can refer to a in the body of the function.
sentences.zh: 紧接着我定义了一个函数，那么我就可以在该函数体内部引用 a。

sentences.en: You can't do that in C.
sentences.zh: 你在 C 语言中是做不到这一点的。

sentences.en: So it, it becomes like, you can't, so you can't like capture the environment that it was in.
sentences.zh: 所以这就变成，你无法做到这一点，所以你无法捕获它当时所处的环境。

sentences.en: So you can't really do the functional stuff.
sentences.zh: 因此你其实无法进行那些函数式的操作。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That makes sense.
sentences.zh: 这很好理解。

sentences.en: So, I mean, I think one analogy is if you've ever played world of Warcraft, um, or any of these, you know, MMOs or many games kind of like it, you know, some of the weapons, you
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我觉得有一个类比，如果你玩过《魔兽世界》，嗯，或者任何此类 MMO 游戏或类似的游戏，你知道，有些武器，

sentences.en: know, in the beginning you get the wooden sword and like, you just hit the rat over and over again.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一开始你拿到一把木剑，然后你就一下又一下地打老鼠。

sentences.en: But then as you get better and better, you get one of these swords that has what's called a proc, which is short for a procedure.
sentences.zh: 但随着你越来越厉害，你会拿到一把带有所谓“触发效果（proc，即 procedure 的简称）”的剑。

sentences.en: So it might be, you know, when you hit somebody, there's a 10% chance of them turning into a chicken or something.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能是，当你击中某人时，有 10% 的概率把他们变成一只鸡之类的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so, you know, that, that process, like that event is sort of tied to that sword.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，那个过程，那个事件就像是和那把剑绑定在一起的。

sentences.en: Like you kind of want to assign the turning into a chicken to that weapon and be able to, if you give the weapon to someone else, you want to sort of give that logic to them too.
sentences.zh: 你有点像是把“变成鸡”这个逻辑赋予了那把武器，而且如果你把这把武器给别人，你也希望把那个逻辑一并传递给他们。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: And so I think, yeah, part of functional programming is this idea that like you can pass these functions around as, as sort of first-class citizens.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，是的，函数式编程的一部分就是这种理念：你可以把这些函数像第一类公民一样四处传递。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's a really, uh, great metaphor there.
sentences.zh: 这个比喻真的非常棒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I played too much World of Warcraft.
sentences.zh: 我《魔兽世界》玩得太多了。

sentences.en: Another way to look at it, um, that, uh, that, that I've heard about is, so you have, if you're familiar with object-oriented programming, you've got objects that have methods.
sentences.zh: 另一种看待它的方式，嗯，我听说过的另一种方式是，如果你熟悉面向对象编程，你就会知道对象带有方法。

sentences.en: So that's data with functions attached.
sentences.zh: 也就是附带了函数的数据。

sentences.en: Well, in, in a closure, in a, in a lexical closure, like in a functional language, you have functions with data attached.
sentences.zh: 而在 Clojure 中，在一个词法闭包中，就像在函数式语言中一样，你拥有的是附带了数据的函数。

sentences.en: So those, that, the, the variables that are defined in the scope are, are the data that you can access from that function.
sentences.zh: 所以那些在作用域中定义的变量，就是你可以从该函数中访问的数据。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这说得通。

sentences.en: So, so that's functional programming and we covered Lisp, uh, in, in the, in the Lisp episode.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是函数式编程，我们在 Lisp 那期节目里讨论过 Lisp。

sentences.en: Um, but, uh, but basically, you know, you know, what is closure?
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过，基本上，你知道，Clojure 到底是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, when we covered closure, we just very superficially said closure is Lisp on the JVM, but, you know, I'm sure it's, it's much more than just that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，当我们讨论 Clojure 时，我们只是非常表面地说 Clojure 是运行在 JVM 上的 Lisp，但，你知道，我确信它远不止于此。

sentences.en: Um, you know, kind of, how does closure fit into this whole landscape?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那么，Clojure 是如何融入整个技术生态的呢？

sentences.en: Oh, uh, good question.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: Well, closure is a Lisp for the JVM and Lisp is cool because it's got, it's like a family, you know, it's like it got dialects.
sentences.zh: 嗯，Clojure 是运行在 JVM 上的 Lisp，而 Lisp 很酷，因为它像是一个家族，你知道，它有很多方言。

sentences.en: And so closure is a dialect of Lisp that is made to be hosted on a virtual machine.
sentences.zh: 所以 Clojure 是 Lisp 的一种方言，旨在托管于虚拟机之上。

sentences.en: Um, and, and JVM is like the, the first virtual machine that it's hosted on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，JVM 就像是它托管的第一个虚拟机。

sentences.en: Oh, I see.
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白了。

sentences.en: Is there, is there something you can't do in closure because of that?
sentences.zh: 因为这个原因，有没有什么是你在 Clojure 里做不到的？

sentences.en: I mean, is it, is there like, because it's a dialect of Lisp, is there, is there some things that aren't there or are there that aren't in regular Lisp?
sentences.zh: 我是说，是不是因为它是 Lisp 的方言，所以有些常规 Lisp 具备的东西它没有，或者有些它有而常规 Lisp 没有？

sentences.en: Um, huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯？

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a different language than say common Lisp.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它与比如 Common Lisp 是一门不同的语言。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of stuff that, uh, comes with common Lisp, um, that is built into the language.
sentences.zh: 所以 Common Lisp 自带了许多功能，嗯，语言本身内置了很多特性。

sentences.en: Whereas in closure, because it's designed to be hosted, uh, it, it just relies on, on what the host can do.
sentences.zh: 而在 Clojure 中，因为它被设计为托管语言，它只是依赖于宿主环境（host）所能做的事情。

sentences.en: Gotcha.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So I'll, I'll give an example.
sentences.zh: 那我举个例子。

sentences.en: Uh, common Lisp has this very sophisticated and like just a lot of features in the exception mechanism.
sentences.zh: Common Lisp 的异常机制非常复杂，且拥有大量功能。

sentences.en: So when you throw an exception, you can actually do what's called a restart.
sentences.zh: 所以当你抛出异常时，你实际上可以执行一种名为“重启（restart）”的操作。

sentences.en: So you catch this exception and you can like fix the problem and then recall it and go right back to where the exception was thrown.
sentences.zh: 也就是说你捕获这个异常，然后你可以修复问题，接着重新调用它，直接回到抛出异常的那一行代码去。

sentences.en: So if like the file is not found, you can be like, Oh, not found.
sentences.zh: 所以如果找不到文件，你可以这样：哦，没找到。

sentences.en: Well, let me make it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我创建一个。

sentences.en: And then you go right back into where it was.
sentences.zh: 然后你就直接回到了原来的地方继续执行。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Oh, cool.
sentences.zh: 哦，太酷了。

sentences.en: Um, whereas in Java and it's just built into the JVM, it's not part of the Java language.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而在 Java 中，这是 JVM 内置的，而不是 Java 语言本身的一部分。

sentences.en: It's, it's part of the virtual machine.
sentences.zh: 它是虚拟机的一部分。

sentences.en: The exception gets thrown and like the call stack gets unwound and it's loSt.
sentences.zh: 当异常被抛出时，调用栈会展开，然后异常就被丢弃了。

sentences.en: Like you can't go back to where you were.
sentences.zh: 就像你无法回到你之前待过的地方一样。

sentences.en: Um, it's just, and, and so closure just kind of borrows all of that stuff from the host that it's on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，Clojure 只是借用了它所运行的宿主环境的所有这些特性。
